terms.name: dbt
terms.definition: dbt is a tool that transforms raw source data into dimensional models using business logic defined in code.

terms.name: SFDC
terms.definition: SFDC refers to Salesforce.com, the customer relationship management (CRM) platform used to manage leads, accounts, and contacts.

terms.name: MQL
terms.definition: A Marketing Qualified Lead (MQL) is a person who meets specific criteria set by Marketing and is considered ready for engagement by Sales Development. At GitLab, MQLs are identified through systematic means and tracked in Salesforce.

terms.name: IP
terms.definition: IP usually stands for Intellectual Property, which refers to creations of the mind like inventions, designs, and trademarks.

terms.name: WIP
terms.definition: WIP means 'Work In Progress' and is used to indicate something is not yet complete or finalized.

terms.name: Marketo
terms.definition: Marketo is a marketing automation platform used to manage programs, sync data with Salesforce, track lead activity, and automate marketing tasks.

terms.name: Pipeline
terms.definition: Pipeline refers to the total value of sales opportunities that are currently in progress and tracked through the sales process.

terms.name: Coupa
terms.definition: Coupa is a procurement and expense management tool used to submit purchase requests and manage suppliers.

terms.name: Tableau
terms.definition: Tableau is a data visualization and business intelligence tool used to build dashboards and reports from data sources like the Enterprise Data Warehouse.

terms.name: GA
terms.definition: GA stands for General Availability, meaning a product or feature is fully released and available for all customers.

terms.name: SAO
terms.definition: An SAO is an opportunity that has been accepted by sales, specifically when it moves from '0-Pending Acceptance' to '1-Discovery' stage and meets required field criteria.

terms.name: FM
terms.definition: FM stands for Field Marketer, a role responsible for regional or field marketing activities.

terms.name: SA
terms.definition: SA refers to Solutions Architect, a role that is added to the Account and Opportunity objects in Salesforce for workload, compensation, and tracking purposes.

terms.name: Bizible
terms.definition: Bizible is a marketing attribution tool (now called Adobe Marketo Measure) used to track and report on marketing touchpoints and their impact on leads and opportunities in Salesforce (SFDC).

terms.name: MDF
terms.definition: Funds provided by GitLab to Channel Partners to support their marketing campaigns and events. Partners must submit an MDF request for approval before being reimbursed.

terms.name: SD
terms.definition: SD is not explicitly defined in the excerpts, but in GTM Ops and sales contexts, SD usually refers to 'Sales Development.'

terms.name: SDR
terms.definition: A Sales Development Representative (SDR) is responsible for qualifying leads, engaging with potential customers, and booking meetings for further sales conversations.

terms.name: MM
terms.definition: MM is not defined in the provided excerpts. In GTM Ops and SaaS industry, MM commonly stands for Mid-Market, referring to a customer segment between SMB and Enterprise.

terms.name: KPI
terms.definition: A measurable value used to track progress toward specific business objectives.

terms.name: GA4
terms.definition: GA4 is the latest version of Google Analytics used to track and analyze website and app events and user interactions.

terms.name: Salesforce
terms.definition: Salesforce is a cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) platform used to manage accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities, and related sales activities.

terms.name: ARR
terms.definition: ARR is the amount of recurring revenue a customer generates in one year from subscriptions or contracts.

terms.name: L2R
terms.definition: L2R refers to models and reports that track the process from initial lead to recognized revenue, analyzing campaign interactions and attribution.

terms.name: FMM
terms.definition: FMM refers to a specific marketing effort or campaign type used to track whether a touchpoint is influenced or sourced by it.

terms.name: Google Analytics
terms.definition: Google Analytics is a web analytics tool used to track and report website traffic and user behavior on GitLab's web properties.

terms.name: MGP
terms.definition: MGP is the dollar value of sales opportunities attributed to marketing activities.

terms.name: AR
terms.definition: ARR is the yearly recurring revenue from subscriptions, used to measure the value of deals and opportunities.

terms.name: UTM
terms.definition: UTM parameters are tags added to URLs to track the source, medium, and campaign of website traffic for analytics purposes.

terms.name: Conversion rate
terms.definition: Conversion rate is the percentage of opportunities or subscriptions that move to the next stage or become closed/won over a period of time.

terms.name: RAW
terms.definition: RAW refers to unprocessed source data as it is ingested, before any transformations or business logic are applied.

terms.name: GTM
terms.definition: GTM refers to the coordinated process of launching new products, SKUs, or offers to field teams and the market, ensuring effective support and alignment with internal processes.

terms.name: FO
terms.definition: FO stands for First Order, referring to the first qualifying paid subscription opportunity for an Ultimate Parent Account (UPA). Only one UPA FO can exist at a time per UPA.

terms.name: CTA
terms.definition: A CTA is a prompt or button that encourages users to take a specific action, such as clicking a link, filling out a form, or engaging further with content.
